nodes.title: Semistable vertex sets, semistable decompositions and the skeleton of a curve
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth connected projective curve over an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field K, X̂ its analytification and X = X̂ minus a finite set D of punctures. A semistable vertex set of X̂ is a finite set V of type-2 points such that X̂^an ∖ V is a disjoint union of open balls and finitely many open annuli; a semistable vertex set of X additionally has the punctures in distinct open-ball components. The skeleton Σ(X, V) = V ∪ ⋃ Σ(A) over the generalized open annuli A of the decomposition; the completed skeleton Σ̂(X, V) is its closure in X̂^an, equal to Σ(X, V) ∪ D, a graph with vertex set V ∪ D whose open edges are the skeleta of the annuli. (Lemma 3.2) The limit boundary of an open ball component is a single vertex; an open annulus component S(a)^+ has σ: (0, r) → A (r = val(a)) extending continuously to [0, r] with endpoints in V (possibly equal); a punctured ball has endpoints one vertex and one puncture. (Lemma 3.4) Σ is closed, compact iff X = X̂; its limit boundary is D; the components of X^an ∖ Σ are open balls with one-point limit boundary in Σ; Σ is the set of points with no affinoid neighbourhood isomorphic to B(1) and disjoint from V.
hypotheses: K algebraically closed and complete with respect to a nontrivial nonarchimedean valuation (the paper's standing assumption); type-2 points; annuli are standard generalized open annuli S(a)^+ with modulus val(a).
Semistable vertex sets of X̂ correspond bijectively to isomorphism classes of semistable formal models (Theorem 4.11, not read).
proofSteps: Lemma 3.2(1): for an open ball A ≅ B(1)^+ define ||f|| = lim_{r→0} ||f||_r for f regular on an affine open containing A (piecewise affine in r with finitely many slope changes by Proposition 2.10); this is a multiplicative norm defining a point x, and the extension of B(1)^+ ∪ {Shilov point} → X^an is continuous by checking neighbourhoods of the Shilov point along an annulus S(a)^+ where f has no zeros (Lemma 2.13); compactness gives closedness of A ∪ {x}.
Lemma 3.4: (1)-(3) follow from Lemma 3.2 and Lemma 2.12 (an annulus minus its skeleton is a union of open balls); (4) uses Proposition 2.4 (skeleton of an annulus).
acceptance: For a curve with good reduction, V = {the Gauss-type point of the reduction} is a semistable vertex set with Σ = V (single vertex; the vertex genus is the genus of the curve).
For a Tate elliptic curve, a minimal semistable vertex set gives a skeleton which is a loop of length −val(j).

nodes.title: The retraction X^an → Σ(X, V) is continuous and the skeleton is connected
nodes.statement: For a semistable vertex set V, define τ_V: X^an → Σ(X, V) by sending x ∉ Σ to the unique limit-boundary point of its component (an open ball) in X^an ∖ Σ, and τ_V = id on Σ. Then τ_V is continuous, restricts on each generalized open annulus A of the decomposition to the retraction τ_A: A → Σ(A), and Σ(X, V) and Σ̂(X, V) are connected.
hypotheses: Continuity at points of V ('τ_V^{-1}(U) contains an open neighbourhood of x for x ∈ V') is left as an exercise in the source.
proofSteps: On annuli τ_V = τ_A is continuous by Lemma 2.12; at vertices the source leaves the check to the reader.
Proposition 3.9: the continuous image of the connected X^an under τ_V is Σ.
acceptance: The retraction of a type-1 point in an open-ball component is the vertex at its limit boundary; refining V by adding a type-2 point in an annulus subdivides an edge and the retractions are compatible.

nodes.title: Existence of semistable vertex sets and characterization of minimal skeleta (statement)
nodes.statement: Theorem 4.22: a semistable vertex set of X exists. If V is a minimal semistable vertex set then (1) if χ(X) ≤ 0, Σ(X, V) is the set of points of X^an with no affinoid neighbourhood isomorphic to B(1); (2) if χ(X) < 0, V is stable and V = {x ∈ Σ(X, V): x is a topological vertex (valence ≥ 3) or g(x) > 0}. Corollary 4.23: for χ(X) ≤ 0 there is a unique set-theoretic minimal skeleton and for χ(X) < 0 a unique stable vertex set.
hypotheses: Existence is deduced from Deligne-Mumford's stable reduction theorem in the analytic form of Bosch-Lutkebohmert [BL85, Theorem 7.1] over a non-noetherian rank-1 valuation ring; the source's proof beyond its first lines was not read.
χ(X) is the Euler characteristic of Definition 4.19 (not read); g(x) is the genus of a type-2 point.
proofSteps: Existence for X̂ from [BL85, Theorem 7.1]; existence for the punctured X by adding vertices separating punctures (proof not read further).
acceptance: A genus ≥ 2 curve has a unique stable vertex set; a Tate curve (χ = 0) has a unique minimal skeleton (the loop) but no unique minimal vertex set.

sources.locator: Section 4, Theorem 4.22 and Corollary 4.23 with the opening of the proof (extraction lines 885-900)
sources.excerpt: Theorem 4.22. (Stable reduction theorem) There exists a semistable vertex set of X. If V is a minimal semistable vertex set of X then: (1) If χ(X) ≤ 0 then Σ(X, V) is the set of points in X^an that do not admit an affinoid neighborhood isomorphic to B(1).

nodes.title: Faithful tropicalization of finite subgraphs and the tropical multiplicity formula (statements)
nodes.statement: Let X be a curve over an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field K and H°(X^an) the set of non-type-1 points with its metric. (Theorem 1.1) For every finite embedded subgraph Γ ⊂ H°(X^an) there is a closed embedding of X into a quasiprojective toric variety, meeting the dense torus T, such that Γ maps isometrically onto its image in Trop(X ∩ T); the set of such embeddings is stable under domination and hence cofinal. (Theorem 1.3) Trop(X ∩ T) has a polyhedral structure such that for each edge e' finitely many segments e_1, ..., e_r of H°(X^an) map homeomorphically onto e', every other segment in the preimage is contracted, and the tropical multiplicity is m_Trop(e') = m_rel(e_1) + ... + m_rel(e_r), where m_rel(e) is the absolute value of the integer slope of the affine map e → e'. (Theorem 1.4) If in_w(X ∩ T) is irreducible and generically reduced for all w in a finite subgraph Γ' ⊂ Trop(X ∩ T), there is a unique embedded subgraph Γ ⊂ H°(X^an) mapping homeomorphically onto Γ', and this map is an isometry. For an affine curve embedded by invertible functions f_1, ..., f_n, m_rel(e) = gcd(s_1(e), ..., s_n(e)) with s_i(e) the slope of log|f_i| along e (Remark 5.6; slopes computable by the slope formula of BPR13 Theorem 5.15).
hypotheses: K algebraically closed and complete; X a curve (smooth? the introduction does not restate the standing hypotheses; the body's assumptions were not read); tropicalization Trop(X ∩ T) is the closure of trop(X(K) ∩ T) with the polyhedral structure of Theorem 4.28.
Proofs (Sections 4-6: polyhedral domains, Theorem 4.30 finiteness of ψ^P, Theorem 5.8 compatibility of multiplicities, Corollary 5.9) were not read.
proofSteps: As described in the introduction: relate expansion factors m_rel(e) to tropical multiplicities through initial degenerations (Corollary 5.9); refine embeddings so that contracted edges or expansion factors > 1 are corrected; stability under domination gives cofinality (Section 5.15 domination order).
acceptance: For an elliptic curve with bad reduction the skeleton loop has length −val(j); a plane model that contracts the loop or has expansion factor > 1 is repaired by a refined embedding, recovering the Katz-Markwig-Markwig tropical j-invariant statements (Example 2.8, Section 6).
If an edge e' has tropical multiplicity 1, there is a unique segment e ⊂ H°(X^an) over it and its length equals the tropical length of e'.

links.reason: The retraction is defined through the open-ball components of X^an ∖ Σ and their one-point limit boundaries (Lemma 3.4(3)).
Theorem 4.22 asserts existence and minimality properties of the objects defined in Section 3.
Faithful tropicalization is stated for finite subgraphs of H°(X^an), whose metric and skeleta come from the semistable decomposition theory of BPR13/BPR14; Theorem 1.3's segments e_i lie in skeleta.
